speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

Your description of constant, low-grade spinning since this morning that improves slightly with diphenhydramine, combined with recent upper respiratory symptoms, points more towards vestibular neuritis or a viral labyrinthitis rather than Meniere's disease. While Meniere's typically presents with fluctuating symptoms over 20 minutes to hours and ear fullness, your sustained continuous vertigo suggests inflammation of the vestibular nerve. Do you have any history of head trauma, and is the nausea your only associated symptom besides the dizziness?
